color.name: --color-surface-50
color.usage: Primitive ramps, renamed 2026-09-07 to match Figma's own families (50 = lightest). Consumed only via the semantic tokens above — no component binds a primitive directly (rules §1). Figma's Event group is deliberately absent: it's print/campaign-only, carries no semantic role, and is recorded in tokens.json rather than registered here, so no Tailwind utility is ever generated for it.

color.name: --color-surface-section
color.usage: The background of anything that is a surface: sections, cards, panels. Set the element's data-mode and this token becomes that surface. Single successor to the retired surface-primary/secondary/tertiary/inverse/feature/subtle/emphasis set — one token, four resolutions.

color.name: --color-surface-card
color.usage: Light cream for elevated surfaces — Modal fills with this. Mode-invariant (Surface/50 in every mode), which is why Modal also sets data-mode="cream" on itself: text-primary only clears AA against this fill in the On Cream column. Cards use surface-section and choose their colour by mode instead.

color.name: --color-surface-scrim-start
color.usage: Top stop of a text-over-image scrim (Card/Producer). Neutral/900 at 0%. Mode-invariant.

color.name: --color-surface-scrim-end
color.usage: Bottom stop of a text-over-image scrim (Card/Producer). Neutral/900 at 85%. Mode-invariant.

color.name: --color-text-primary
color.usage: Headings, body and icons. Icons bind this too — the icon-* group is retired and icons use the matching text-* token.

color.name: --color-text-secondary
color.usage: Supporting text, captions and metadata. Absorbed the retired text-muted.

color.name: --color-text-link
color.usage: Inline links, link buttons and interactive icons. Absorbed the retired text-highlight and text-button.

color.name: --color-text-on-action
color.usage: Text and icons on an action-primary fill (Button primary's label). Flips in lockstep with action-primary — the pairing measures 11.45:1 in every mode.

color.name: --color-text-on-highlight
color.usage: Text on an action-highlight fill (Button accent's label). Mode-invariant — always Neutral/800, since every mode's accent fill is a mid-to-light amber.

color.name: --color-text-on-state
color.usage: Text on a state-* fill (Badge's success/warning/error variants). Mode-invariant, matching those fills, which are the same colour on every surface.

color.name: --color-action-primary
color.usage: Primary button fill. Dark on cream, light on the three dark surfaces.

color.name: --color-action-primary-hover
color.usage: Primary button fill on hover.

color.name: --color-action-secondary
color.usage: Secondary (outlined) button and Input-family field fill — genuinely transparent (Alpha/White-0), not white. Mode-invariant: the surface behind it showing through is the point. Always compute contrast against the composited result, never against this token alone.

color.name: --color-action-secondary-hover
color.usage: Secondary button and Input-family hover tint — a 10%-alpha wash baked into the token, ink-tinted on cream and white-tinted on the three dark surfaces. Successor to the retired state-hover.

color.name: --color-action-highlight
color.usage: Accent button fill. Mode-variant as of 2026-09-07 — it was pinned to a single amber under the previous architecture.

color.name: --color-action-highlight-hover
color.usage: Accent button fill on hover.

color.name: --color-action-disabled
color.usage: Standalone disabled fill, for disabled text and surfaces outside a component. Components never use it — a disabled control is its Default appearance at opacity-disabled, never a colour swap (rules §2).

color.name: --color-border-default
color.usage: Dividers and the resting border on Input-family controls. Same colour as text-secondary in every mode, by design in Figma.

color.name: --color-border-strong
color.usage: Outlined buttons, Badge's neutral outline, Tab's active indicator, and any emphasised rule. Same colour as text-primary in every mode.

color.name: --color-border-subtle
color.usage: 10% ink hairline for card edges, table rows and section rules.

color.name: --color-state-focus
color.usage: Focus ring — 2px, offset 2px outside the control (rules §2). Successor to border-focus and its retired -inverse/-on-feature/-on-highlight partners. Focus/500 on cream, Focus/200 on the three dark surfaces; clears SC 1.4.11's 3:1 on all four (4.40 / 6.08 / 8.92 / 3.67).

color.name: --color-state-error
color.usage: Error text, borders and badge fills. Mode-invariant — a status colour means the same thing on every surface, and pairs with text-on-state at 6.28:1.

color.name: --color-state-success
color.usage: Success text, borders and badge fills. Mode-invariant; pairs with text-on-state at 6.92:1.

color.name: --color-state-warning
color.usage: Warning text, borders and badge fills. Rebound to Accent/950 in the 2026-09-07 sync (was a mode-variant amber); pairs with text-on-state at 6.97:1.

color.name: --color-state-disabled
color.usage: Disabled text and icons standing alone, outside a component. Absorbed the retired icon-disabled.

typography.name: --text-label
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Label" — Badge's label at both sizes.

typography.name: --text-h6
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/H6" — Button's large-size label, and the large-size value/label text for every Input-family control.

typography.name: --text-paragraph-small
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Paragraph Small" — Card/Event's date, time and description, Card/Producer's location, Tab's label, and the small-size value/label text for every Input-family control.

typography.name: --text-h3
typography.usage: Figma text style "Recoleta/H3" — Card/Event's title and Card/Quote's quote, the two places the Recoleta display face carries a block of copy.

typography.name: --text-label-strong
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Label SemiBold". AUTO line-height in Figma, not a fixed ratio — "normal" matches Figma's own setting rather than hand-computing a ratio off one rendered sample. Weight (600) isn't encoded here, same convention as every other --text-* token — apply font-semibold alongside. Landing page's Hero eyebrow and the floating date card's time line.

typography.name: --text-paragraph-large
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Paragraph Large" — landing page's Hero description paragraph.

typography.name: --text-caption
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Caption" — Card/Quote's attribution, Modal's description, and the landing page's Footer tagline.

typography.name: --text-overline
typography.usage: Figma text style "Manrope/Overline Compact" — Card/Producer's category label and the landing page's floating date card "SATURDAY" label. Also carries a real 3px letter-spacing, unlike every other --text-* token here: Tailwind v4 supports a --text-*--letter-spacing companion the same way it supports --line-height, so it's captured as a token property rather than left to an ad hoc tracking-[3px] utility. Weight (600) still isn't encoded here, same convention as every other --text-* token.

typography.name: --text-h4
typography.usage: Figma text style "Recoleta/H4" — Card/Producer's name and the landing page's floating date card's date line.

spacing.name: --spacing-10
spacing.usage: px, not rem — see spacing-00's comment above for why.

spacing.name: --spacing-00
spacing.usage: px, not rem: the host app sets root font-size to 18px (see index.css), which would otherwise scale every rem-based Tailwind utility 1.125x off its nominal value. Design tokens must stay pixel-exact regardless of the host's font-size choice. Repeated on every step below (not left to bleed across the ramp by adjacency) — see design-sync.js's extractCssTokenComments for why a comment no longer implicitly covers more than the one token directly beneath it.

motion.name: --duration-standard / --ease-standard
motion.usage: Not Figma-sourced — the file has no motion variables and the 2026-09-07 export carries no motion group. Formalizes the identical transition-colors duration-150 ease-out already used across Button and the Input family.

breakpoint.name: --breakpoint-tablet
breakpoint.usage: Not Figma-sourced (no breakpoint variables exist in the file) and not used by any built component (none are responsive). Formalizes the one breakpoint value already used across the pre-existing app shell (src/index.css, src/App.css). Tailwind's own default scale is available but not adopted by this system.
